# Colecto v0.1.0 — first alpha

Colecto is an extensible email client with a Rust mail daemon, a Svelte interface,
and a Tauri native shell. This is the first alpha release; expect rough edges.

## Features

- Connect multiple IMAP/SMTP or JMAP accounts, with credentials protected by an
  operating system keyring or a master password.
- Read and search mail, compose and persist drafts, send messages, and manage
  local labels.
- Arrange the workspace with dockable panes, message tabs, keyboard shortcuts,
  and a command palette.
- Customize the dark interface and notification preferences.
- Use bundled interface extensions or install isolated WebAssembly panels with
  explicit capabilities.
- Run the standalone daemon under systemd or another supervisor, or host it with
  Docker and connect clients over HTTPS.
- Automate mail through scoped API keys and MCP, with approval before sending.

## Installation and limits

See [installation instructions](https://github.com/hexvale-labs/colecto/blob/v0.1.0/docs/install.md)
and [daemon hosting](https://github.com/hexvale-labs/colecto/blob/v0.1.0/docs/docker.md).
Arch packaging includes source, binary, and development package recipes; AUR
publication requires the maintainer's configured SSH key.

Apple DMGs and IPAs are experimental artifacts. macOS downloads lack Developer ID
signing and notarization; iOS artifacts require signing and provisioning before
installation. These platforms are not supported. Android device behavior still
needs physical-device validation.

Mail storage is not encrypted. This alpha is designed for one owner's accounts;
multi-user hosting and cross-device synchronization are not implemented.
